extracted.intended_audience: OEIS contributors, editors, and mathematicians who submit or use OEIS entries
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for composing, formatting, and classifying entries in the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS). Includes conventions, required/optional entry fields, keyword taxonomy, numbering/offset rules, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions (notation and character set)
rubrics_metrics.description: OEIS uses plain ASCII text and a linear form of conventional mathematical notation (e.g. f(n), n for running variables). Greek letters are usually spelled out (mu for μ, phi for φ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual terms separated by commas; digit groups are not separated; use a(n) to denote the nth term. Historically limited to ASCII until 2011 and still follows linear notation. Examples: use 'a(n)' not subscripted notation; spell greek names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence identifier (A-number / ID number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every sequence has a serial number: the letter 'A' followed by six digits (zero-padded when appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-numbers are assigned by editors or via an 'A number dispenser' for multiple related submissions; a dispenser-reserved A-number expires one month if unused. Legacy M- and N-numbers (from predecessor books) are kept in parentheses when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence field (data length and B-files)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence field lists the numbers themselves to about 260 characters; more terms should be provided in B-files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence field makes no automatic distinction between long finite and infinite sequences; use keywords 'fini', 'full', and 'more' to denote finite/complete/want-more status. To determine indexing, use the offset field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offset field
rubrics_metrics.description: Offset is the index n of the first term given; default offset is 0 (many sequences use 0 or 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some sequences may have nonstandard offsets (e.g. 3 or −1) depending on context. Internally OEIS stores two offset numbers: the public offset and a second index indicating the first entry (counting from 1) whose absolute value exceeds 1 — used to speed searching. Contributors should check that default offset is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name field
rubrics_metrics.description: The name field contains the most common name for the sequence and sometimes the formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a common name exists, put it here; formulaic names (e.g. 'The cubes: a(n)=n^3') are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments field (purpose and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are for information about the sequence that doesn't fit other fields, often relationships, applications, or observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comments to point out connections to other sequences, unexpected applications, clarifications about offsets/definitions, or known properties. Examples are provided in the entry A000578 and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: References field
rubrics_metrics.description: References should list printed documents (books, papers) relevant to the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conventional bibliographic references when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links field
rubrics_metrics.description: Links are URLs to online resources related to the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links may point to journal articles, index pages, text files of term lists (two-column), images showing combinatorial background, or code repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula field
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains formulas, recurrences, generating functions, etc. that define or characterize the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include closed forms, recurrences, Dirichlet/generating functions, and any known analytic descriptions. Examples and references help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example field
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives worked examples showing how particular terms are obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide short illustrative computations (e.g. a(3) computed from divisor sums) to help readers verify terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program fields (Maple/Mathematica/PARI/other code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields for programs to compute the sequence in Maple, Mathematica (Wolfram Language), PARI/GP, and other languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEIS historically preferred Maple and Mathematica; as of 2016 many Mathematica programs exist followed by PARI/GP, Maple, and other languages. Program entries should indicate the author of the code; if no name, the submitter is assumed to be the program author. Note: OEIS policy on displaying e-mail addresses changed (post-2011 they are not shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossrefs field
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references (denoted 'Cf.') link the entry to related sequences and indicate its context (lexicographic neighbors and related A-numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sequences closely related by formula, definition, or lexicographic adjacency; provide 'see also' links and context listing where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords field (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: OEIS uses a standard lexicon of mostly four-letter keywords to characterize sequences (e.g. 'core', 'mult', 'fini', ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign appropriate keywords to indicate properties, interest level, computability, format, and other metadata. Many keywords have specific definitions and usage rules (see individual keyword entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: allocated
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-number has been set aside for a user but the entry has not yet been approved or written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when contributors request a block of A-numbers for related sequences; dispenser allocations expire if not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: base
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of the calculation or the characterization depend on a specific positional base (e.g. palindromes in base 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'base' when a sequence's definition or property is base-dependent; some sequences might not rate 'base' if defined invariantly (e.g. Mersenne primes as 2^n−1 do not rate 'base').

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: bref
rubrics_metrics.description: 'sequence is too short to do any analysis with' — indicates very short sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when there are insufficient terms to analyze or infer deeper properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: changed
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence has been changed in the last two weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by the web form or by editorial action to flag recently edited entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: cofr
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence represents a continued fraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'cofr' for continued fraction expansions (distinct from 'frac' which denotes rational-number numerator/denominator sequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: cons
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence is a decimal (or other) expansion of a mathematical constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'cons' for expansions of constants such as e or π (cf. 'cons' examples A001113, A000796).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: core
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence of foundational importance to a branch of mathematics (e.g. primes, Fibonacci).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjective but reserved for sequences with broad foundational significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: dead
rubrics_metrics.description: Used for erroneous sequences that have appeared in the literature or duplicates of existing sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark known incorrect or duplicated sequences as 'dead' to indicate they should not be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: dumb
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective label for 'unimportant sequences', often trivial, pop-culture, or non-mathematical sequences kept mainly for trivia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include arbitrary internet-puzzle sequences or novelty sequences (e.g. A085808). Use judiciously; editorial discretion applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: easy
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms of the sequence can be easily calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often applied to simple arithmetic sequences or functions defined by an easy-to-evaluate formula; note 'easy' is mutually exclusive with 'hard'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: eigen
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence of eigenvalues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply where sequence corresponds to eigenvalues of matrices/operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: fini
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence is finite (possibly displayed in full or truncated in the main field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'fini' is used and the full list is displayed, also use 'full'. Example: supersingular primes (finite known list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: frac
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence of numerators or denominators of a sequence of fractions representing rational numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequences of fractions should be represented by two sequences (keyword 'frac'): one for numerators and one for denominators. Do not use 'frac' for continued fractions (use 'cofr').

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: full
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence field displays the complete sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with 'fini' — 'full' implies the entire finite sequence is shown. 'full' is mutually exclusive with 'more'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: hard
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms of the sequence cannot be easily calculated, even with brute force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to sequences tied to unsolved problems or computationally difficult enumerations (mutually exclusive with 'easy').

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: hear
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence has an audio/graphical representation deemed particularly interesting or beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for sequences with noteworthy audio/visual renders; OEIS collects examples labeled 'hear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: less
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A less interesting sequence' — subjective lower-interest label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'less' is considered somewhat subjective and is mutually exclusive with 'nice'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: look
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence has a graph visual deemed particularly interesting or beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for sequences whose plotted graphs have aesthetic or informative value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: more
rubrics_metrics.description: More terms of the sequence are wanted (the current list is insufficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag sequences where readers/contributors are encouraged to submit extensions; 'more' is mutually exclusive with 'full'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: mult
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence corresponds to a multiplicative arithmetic function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term a(1) should be 1; a(mn)=a(m)a(n) when m,n are coprime. Provide multiplicative factorization examples when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: new
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence added or majorly extended in the last couple of weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'new' is added automatically by Sloane's program under applicable conditions and is not a web-form checkbox for submitters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: nice
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective label for 'exceptionally nice sequences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'nice' indicates notable elegance or importance; mutually exclusive with 'less'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: nonn
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence consists of nonnegative integers (may include zeros).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No distinction is made between sequences that are nonnegative due to offset or by definition. 'nonn' is mutually exclusive with 'sign'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: obsc
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence is considered obscure and needs a better definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when description/definition is inadequate or unclear; encourages clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: recycled
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor left only the keyword line with 'recycled' indicating the proposed sequence is not worth adding; the A-number becomes available again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when editors decide to free up an assigned A-number rather than keep a weak entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: sign
rubrics_metrics.description: Some or all values of the sequence are negative; entry includes a Signed field and Sequence field uses absolute values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when sequence contains negative values; 'sign' is mutually exclusive with 'nonn'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: tabf
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregular (funny-shaped) array read row by row to form a sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'tabf' for sequences generated by reading irregular arrays; provide context on the original array shape when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: tabl
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence obtained by reading a geometric arrangement (e.g., triangle) row by row (e.g., Pascal's triangle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when sequence arises from a standard array/table; provide notation for how rows are read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: uned
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence has not been edited but could be worth including and may contain errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag entries needing editorial attention; contributors are encouraged to edit these sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: unkn
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Little is known' about the sequence; no formula or properties known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for sequences with minimal information — encourages further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: walk
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts walks or self-avoiding paths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to combinatorial path-counting sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword: word
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence depends on words of a specific language (e.g., letter counts of English names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for sequences derived from linguistic properties; give language context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual exclusivity of some keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Some keywords are explicitly mutually exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutually exclusive pairs include: core vs dumb; easy vs hard; full vs more; less vs nice; nonn vs sign. Ensure only one of each exclusive pair is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: ID dispenser expiry and legacy numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-number dispenser can allocate numbers that expire after one month if unused; older book numbering (M- and N- numbers) are preserved in ID field when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting multiple related sequences, use the dispenser carefully; include legacy M/N numbers in parentheses for sequences from predecessor books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author(s) field conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Author(s) of a sequence are the submitter(s); names are given as first name, middle initials, last name; e-mail addresses were printed prior to 2011 but are not displayed now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For most sequences after A055000 the author field includes the date of submission. Do not expect e-mail addresses to be shown post-policy change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension field
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists names (and dates) of people who extended or corrected the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to acknowledge contributors who added terms or corrections after original submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexicographic ordering normalization for context
rubrics_metrics.description: OEIS maintains lexicographic order of sequences (each sequence has predecessor and successor); normalization usually ignores initial zeros and ones and the sign of each element for ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization rules affect 'context' listings and adjacency; be aware when determining where a sequence sits in the lexicographic order and when creating crossrefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special sentinel values (zero and -1) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Zero is often used to represent non-existent sequence elements; other sentinel values like −1 are also used in some sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document sentinel usage in comments or definition (e.g. a(n)=0 if no object exists), and provide mathematical justification when applicable (examples provided such as totient valence function A014197).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry completeness and keyword implications (full/fini/more)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use keywords 'fini' and 'full' to indicate finite sequences displayed completely; use 'more' to request additional terms when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing these keywords communicates expectations about completeness and whether contributors should submit more terms. 'full' implies 'fini'; 'more' suggests the main field is partial.
